<task>
Marcus Ade (customer C-200) has emailed about order O-2003. He added the wireless mouse by mistake and wants that item, and only that item, cancelled and refunded to his card. The rest of the order should still ship as planned.
</task>

You are the planning step. You have no tools here: think the task through and write the plan only.

Produce an ordered list of at most 8 steps for an executor who will have the full toolset. Each step must be one concrete action, specific enough to carry out without guessing, and must include any check that has to happen before it. Add a short rationale for the approach.

toolInput.rationale: We must verify the order's current state and identify the wireless mouse line before acting, since policy requires checking status/amount paid before cancel/refund. Only the mouse line should be touched (cancel, refund to card, restock); other lines must remain untouched and proceed to ship normally.
steps: Call get_order for O-2003 to review all lines, statuses, and amounts paid, and identify the line ID for the wireless mouse item.
Confirm the wireless mouse line has not yet shipped (status pending/not shipped); if it has already shipped, stop and inform the user it cannot be cancelled per policy.
Call cancel_order on O-2003 with lineIds=[the wireless mouse line ID] and a reason like 'customer added by mistake', leaving all other lines untouched.
Call restock_item for the wireless mouse product ID with the exact quantity from the cancelled line, referencing orderId O-2003.
Call refund_order for O-2003 with lineIds=[the wireless mouse line ID], amountCents equal to the exact amount paid for that line (from step 1), and method=card.
Call get_order again on O-2003 to confirm the mouse line shows as cancelled/refunded and all other lines remain active/unaffected.
Reply to the user confirming the wireless mouse was cancelled, restocked, and refunded to the original card, and that the rest of the order will ship as planned.
